items.q: Find the determinant of [[-3, 4], [-3, 1]].
items.s: For a two by two arrangement the number is (-3)(1) - (4)(-3) = 9.

items.q: Find the determinant of [[6, 5, 3], [7, 7, 5], [0, 0, 0]].
items.s: The last row is entirely zero, so the determinant is 0.

items.q: Solve for x and y from 2x + 5y = 7 together with y = 2, and state the value of 2x + 5y.
items.s: Substituting y = 2 gives 2x = -3, so x = -1.5 and the expression equals 7.

items.q: The reduced form of a 4 by 5 arrangement has 3 nonzero rows. The remaining rows are entirely zero. State the rank.
items.s: The rank is the number of nonzero rows in the reduced form, which is 3.

items.q: State the dimension of the space of all arrangements with 3 rows and 1 columns.
items.s: Every entry can be chosen freely, so there are 3 x 1 = 3 independent entries.

items.q: A space has dimension 4 and a collection of 4 members is given. State the number of members a basis of the space must contain.
items.s: Every basis of a space of dimension 4 contains exactly 4 members.

items.q: A two by two arrangement has eigenvalues 4 and 1. State the trace of the arrangement.
items.s: The trace equals the total of the eigenvalues, which is 5.

items.q: Under the usual rule the number assigned to the members (-3, 2, 4) and (5, 3, 2) is the sum of the products of matching coordinates. Find that number.
items.s: Multiplying matching coordinates and adding gives -1.

items.q: Given A = [[3, 3, 7], [-5, 4, -2]], find the entry in row 1 and column 1 of the transpose of A.
items.s: The transpose writes rows as columns, so the entry asked for is the one in row 1 and column 1 of A, which is 3.

items.q: Given A = [[3, -2], [3, -1]] and the identity I of order two, find the top left entry of A + 2I.
items.s: Only the diagonal is touched, so the top left entry is 3 + 2 = 5.
The product is diagonal with entries 54, 64, 48, so its trace is their total 166.

items.q: Find the determinant of [[1, -3, 2], [0, 4, 0], [0, 3, 4]].
items.s: Expanding along the first column leaves 1 times the two by two number 4 x 4, giving 16.

items.q: A two by two arrangement A has determinant -4. Find the determinant of 3A.
items.s: Scaling every row of a two by two arrangement multiplies the number by 3^2, so the answer is -12.

items.q: Find the determinant of the upper triangular arrangement [[5, 7, 2], [0, 2, 5], [0, 0, 5]].
items.s: For a triangular arrangement the number is the product of the diagonal entries, here 50.

items.q: Two square arrangements A and B of the same order have determinants 3 and 4. Find the determinant of AB.
items.s: The number attached to a product is the product of the numbers, so it is 12.

items.q: Find the top left entry of the inverse of [[4, 2], [1, 2]].
items.s: The determinant is 6, and the top left entry of the inverse is 2/6 = 0.3333.

items.q: Find the bottom left entry of the inverse of [[1, 1], [1, 4]].
items.s: The bottom left entry of the undoing arrangement is minus the lower left entry over the determinant 3, giving -0.3333.

items.q: A two by two arrangement has determinant -3. Find the determinant of its inverse.
items.s: The number attached to the undoing arrangement is the reciprocal of -3, which is -0.3333.

items.q: A system is written as [[2, 1], [3, 5]] times the column of unknowns equals a column of constants. Find the determinant of the coefficient arrangement and so decide whether the system has a unique solution; state that determinant.
items.s: The determinant is (2)(5) - (1)(3) = 7, and a nonzero value means the solution is unique.

items.q: A system with coefficient arrangement [[2, 4], [2, 3]] has right hand column (3, 8). Using the determinant method, find the first unknown.
items.s: The first unknown is (3 x 3 - 4 x 8)/-2 = 11.5.

items.q: A homogeneous system of three equations in three unknowns has coefficient arrangement of determinant 4. State the value of the unknowns in the only solution it can have when the determinant is nonzero.
items.s: With a nonzero determinant the homogeneous system has only the trivial solution, so every unknown is 0.

items.q: An arrangement has 5 columns and its reduced form has 2 nonzero rows. State its nullity.
items.s: Nullity = columns - rank = 5 - 2 = 3.

items.q: A space has dimension 4 and a collection of 5 members of it is given. State the largest rank the arrangement formed by taking those members as columns can have.
items.s: A collection of 5 members in a space of dimension 4 cannot have rank more than 4, so the largest possible rank is 4.

items.q: State the dimension of the space of all polynomials of degree at most 4 together with the zero polynomial.
items.s: A basis is 1, x, and so on up to x^4, which is 5 members.

items.q: A part of a space consists of all members whose first coordinate equals 3 times the second. State whether it is a subspace by giving the number 1 for yes and 0 for no.
items.s: The condition is preserved by addition and by scaling, and the zero member satisfies it, so the part is a subspace, recorded as 1.

items.q: The list (10, 5) is written in the basis whose first member is (2, 0). Find the first coordinate in that basis.
items.s: The first basis member has zero second coordinate, so the first coordinate is 10/4 = 2.5.

items.q: Two members of the plane have coordinates (4, 5) and (3, 4). State 1 if they are independent and 0 if they are dependent.
items.s: The test value 4 x 4 - 5 x 3 = 1 is nonzero, so the two members are independent, recorded as 1.

items.q: A two by two arrangement has eigenvalues 4 and 3. State its determinant.
items.s: The determinant equals the product of the eigenvalues, which is 12.

items.q: The characteristic expression of a two by two arrangement is L^2 - 8L + 12, where L stands for the unknown number. State the smaller of the two values it produces when set to zero.
items.s: The expression factorises with roots 2 and 6, so the smaller is 2.

items.q: A two by two arrangement has one eigenvalue equal to -3 and the other equal to 3. State the trace of the arrangement.
items.s: The trace is the total of the two values, which is 0.

items.q: The arrangement [[4, 0], [0, 5]] is applied to the column (1, 0). State the factor by which the result is a multiple of the original column.
items.s: The first coordinate is multiplied by 4 and the second stays zero, so the factor is 4.

items.q: A diagonal two by two arrangement has both diagonal entries equal to 3. Find the trace of its 4th power.
items.s: Each diagonal entry of the power is 3^4 = 81, so the trace is twice that, 162.

items.q: A two by two arrangement has eigenvalues 2 and 5. Find the determinant of its 3th power.
items.s: The eigenvalues of the power are 2^3 and 5^3, so the determinant is their product 1000.

items.q: A square arrangement of order 3 has 3 distinct eigenvalues. State how many independent members belonging to those values exist in total.
items.s: Distinct values of a square arrangement of order 3 supply one independent member each, so 3 in all.

items.q: Find the norm of the member (3, 4, 12) under the usual rule.
items.s: The norm is the square root of the sum of squares 169, which is 13.

items.q: The member (10, 8, 8) lies along the direction (5, 4, 4). Find the scalar multiple that expresses it in terms of that direction.
items.s: Matching coordinates are all 2 times as large, so the multiple is 2.

items.q: State the number assigned by the usual rule to the members (1, 1, 0) and (1, -1, 0).
items.s: The products of matching coordinates are 1 and -1, whose total is 0, so the two members are orthogonal.

items.q: Find the largest value that the pairing number of the member (6, 0, 0) with any member of length 12.65 can take, giving the answer to three decimal places.
items.s: The length of the given member is 6, and by the Cauchy inequality the largest pairing number is the product of the lengths, 6 x 12.65 = 75.89.

items.q: Given A = [[-4, -1], [2, 4]] and B = [[3, 6], [2, -3]], find the top left entry of AB.
items.s: The top left entry is row one of A times column one of B: -4 x 3 + -1 x 2 = -14.

items.q: Find the determinant of [[2, 4, 3], [3, 6, 5], [0, 0, 0]].
items.s: The last row is entirely zero, so the determinant is 0.

items.q: Solve for x and y from 2x + 3y = 15 together with y = 1, and state the value of 2x + 3y.
items.s: Substituting y = 1 gives 2x = 12, so x = 6 and the expression equals 15.

items.q: State the dimension of the space of all arrangements with 3 rows and 2 columns.
items.s: Every entry can be chosen freely, so there are 3 x 2 = 6 independent entries.

items.q: A two by two arrangement has eigenvalues 1 and 1. State the trace of the arrangement.
items.s: The trace equals the total of the eigenvalues, which is 2.

items.q: Under the usual rule the number assigned to the members (5, 5, -4) and (2, 1, 5) is the sum of the products of matching coordinates. Find that number.
items.s: Multiplying matching coordinates and adding gives -5.

items.q: Given A = [[1, 5, 9], [-4, 5, 0]], find the entry in row 2 and column 2 of the transpose of A.
items.s: The transpose writes rows as columns, so the entry asked for is the one in row 2 and column 2 of A, which is 5.

items.q: Given A = [[2, -4], [0, 1]] and the identity I of order two, find the top left entry of A + -2I.
items.s: Only the diagonal is touched, so the top left entry is 2 + -2 = 0.
The product is diagonal with entries 35, 4, 21, so its trace is their total 60.

items.q: Find the determinant of [[1, -3, 2], [0, 3, 0], [0, 1, 3]].
items.s: Expanding along the first column leaves 1 times the two by two number 3 x 3, giving 9.

items.q: A two by two arrangement A has determinant -4. Find the determinant of 2A.
items.s: Scaling every row of a two by two arrangement multiplies the number by 2^2, so the answer is -8.

items.q: Find the determinant of the upper triangular arrangement [[3, 7, 2], [0, 3, 5], [0, 0, 6]].
items.s: For a triangular arrangement the number is the product of the diagonal entries, here 54.

items.q: Two square arrangements A and B of the same order have determinants 2 and -3. Find the determinant of AB.
items.s: The number attached to a product is the product of the numbers, so it is -6.

items.q: Find the top left entry of the inverse of [[3, 3], [2, 4]].
items.s: The determinant is 6, and the top left entry of the inverse is 4/6 = 0.6667.

items.q: Find the bottom left entry of the inverse of [[5, 1], [2, 5]].
items.s: The bottom left entry of the undoing arrangement is minus the lower left entry over the determinant 23, giving -0.087.

items.q: A two by two arrangement has determinant -12. Find the determinant of its inverse.
items.s: The number attached to the undoing arrangement is the reciprocal of -12, which is -0.0833.

items.q: A system is written as [[4, 1], [2, 5]] times the column of unknowns equals a column of constants. Find the determinant of the coefficient arrangement and so decide whether the system has a unique solution; state that determinant.
items.s: The determinant is (4)(5) - (1)(2) = 18, and a nonzero value means the solution is unique.

items.q: A system with coefficient arrangement [[3, 2], [3, 3]] has right hand column (5, 7). Using the determinant method, find the first unknown.
items.s: The first unknown is (5 x 3 - 2 x 7)/3 = 0.3333.

items.q: An arrangement has 3 columns and its reduced form has 1 nonzero rows. State its nullity.
items.s: Nullity = columns - rank = 3 - 1 = 2.

items.q: A space has dimension 3 and a collection of 4 members of it is given. State the largest rank the arrangement formed by taking those members as columns can have.
items.s: A collection of 4 members in a space of dimension 3 cannot have rank more than 3, so the largest possible rank is 3.

items.q: State the dimension of the space of all polynomials of degree at most 2 together with the zero polynomial.
items.s: A basis is 1, x, and so on up to x^2, which is 3 members.

items.q: The list (8, 4) is written in the basis whose first member is (2, 0). Find the first coordinate in that basis.
items.s: The first basis member has zero second coordinate, so the first coordinate is 8/4 = 2.

items.q: All of the following belong to Eigenvalues and eigenvectors EXCEPT
o: eigenvector
eigenvalue
diagonalisation
characteristic polynomial
items.s: Every other option belongs to Eigenvalues and eigenvectors. “diagonalisation” belongs to Diagonalisation, not Eigenvalues and eigenvectors.

items.q: Which term is described by “two members whose assigned number under the pairing rule is zero”?
o: Cauchy inequality
orthogonal projection
orthogonal members
norm of a member
items.s: orthogonal members is two members whose assigned number under the pairing rule is zero.

items.q: Which term is described by “a simplified arrangement in which each leading entry lies to the right of the one above it”?
o: rank nullity relation
elementary row operation
rank
row echelon form
items.s: row echelon form is a simplified arrangement in which each leading entry lies to the right of the one above it.

items.q: Which term is described by “a square arrangement whose entries off the leading diagonal are all zero”?
o: skew symmetric array
square array
diagonal array
conformable pair
items.s: diagonal array is a square arrangement whose entries off the leading diagonal are all zero.

items.q: The statement “the number formed from all the pairwise assigned numbers of a collection, testing independence” describes which of the following?
o: inner product
Gram determinant
orthonormal collection
norm of a member
items.s: Gram determinant is the number formed from all the pairwise assigned numbers of a collection, testing independence.

items.q: Which term is described by “a square arrangement that can be written as a basis array sandwiched around a diagonal one”?
o: distinct value condition
diagonalisation
diagonalisable arrangement
defective arrangement
items.s: diagonalisable arrangement is a square arrangement that can be written as a basis array sandwiched around a diagonal one.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines geometric multiplicity?
o: the dimension of the part formed by the members belonging to one value
the first nonzero entry in a row of a simplified array, used to clear the entries beneath it
two arrangements whose inner counts agree, so that they may be multiplied in that order
the statement that a member of a spanning collection can be swapped for an outside member and still span
items.s: geometric multiplicity: the dimension of the part formed by the members belonging to one value. The other options describe pivot, conformable pair, exchange lemma.

items.q: Which term is described by “a square arrangement that cannot be written in diagonal sandwich form because some value lacks enough members”?
o: defective arrangement
similar arrangements
diagonalisable arrangement
distinct value condition
items.s: defective arrangement is a square arrangement that cannot be written in diagonal sandwich form because some value lacks enough members.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines zero member?
o: a nonzero member that a given arrangement merely stretches or reverses
a square arrangement that is its own undoing arrangement
the square root of the number the member is assigned with itself
the unique element that leaves every element unchanged when added to it
items.s: zero member: the unique element that leaves every element unchanged when added to it. The other options describe involutory arrangement, norm of a member, eigenvector.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines exchange lemma?
o: the total of the entries on the leading diagonal of a square arrangement
the statement that a member of a spanning collection can be swapped for an outside member and still span
the part of the space formed by the zero member together with all members belonging to one value
the number formed from all the pairwise assigned numbers of a collection, testing independence
items.s: exchange lemma: the statement that a member of a spanning collection can be swapped for an outside member and still span. The other options describe Gram determinant, eigenspace, trace.

items.q: Which term is described by “the part consisting of the zero member alone”?
o: subspace
closed under addition
trivial subspace
zero member
items.s: trivial subspace is the part consisting of the zero member alone.

items.q: orthogonal arrangement may be defined as
o: the total of the entries on the leading diagonal of a square arrangement
a set of conditions that no set of values can satisfy together
a square arrangement whose transpose is also its undoing arrangement
the dimension of the part formed by the members belonging to one value
items.s: orthogonal arrangement: a square arrangement whose transpose is also its undoing arrangement. The other options describe inconsistent system, trace, geometric multiplicity.

items.q: spectrum may be defined as
o: the whole collection of values attached to an arrangement
the situation in which a square arrangement has two equal rows and so carries the number zero
the arrangement whose columns are the old coordinates of the new basis members
the total of the entries on the leading diagonal of a square arrangement
items.s: spectrum: the whole collection of values attached to an arrangement. The other options describe change of basis array, trace, vanishing condition.

items.q: characteristic polynomial may be defined as
o: the statement that the assigned number of a pair never exceeds the product of the two lengths
the relation between two arrangements that can be turned into each other by allowed row changes
a set of conditions that has at least one set of values satisfying them all
the expression in a single symbol obtained by subtracting that symbol from the diagonal before taking the number
items.s: characteristic polynomial: the expression in a single symbol obtained by subtracting that symbol from the diagonal before taking the number. The other options describe consistent system, Cauchy inequality, row equivalence.

items.q: consistent system may be defined as
o: a set of conditions that has at least one set of values satisfying them all
the count of columns without a leading entry in the simplified form
a square arrangement in which every entry on one side of the leading diagonal is zero
the property that combining any two members of the set stays inside it
items.s: consistent system: a set of conditions that has at least one set of values satisfying them all. The other options describe triangular array, nullity, closed under addition.

items.q: row equivalence may be defined as
o: the relation between two arrangements that can be turned into each other by allowed row changes
a square arrangement with ones on the leading diagonal and zeros elsewhere
the arrangement whose columns are the old coordinates of the new basis members
a set of conditions in which every right hand value is zero
items.s: row equivalence: the relation between two arrangements that can be turned into each other by allowed row changes. The other options describe homogeneous system, change of basis array, identity array.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines rank nullity relation.
o: the count of members in any basis of the space
a square array that is unchanged when its rows and columns are interchanged
a line through the origin that a given arrangement maps onto itself
the statement that the count of columns equals the number of leading entries plus the count of columns without one
items.s: rank nullity relation: the statement that the count of columns equals the number of leading entries plus the count of columns without one. The other options describe invariant direction, dimension, symmetric array.

items.q: The statement “a square arrangement whose transpose is also its undoing arrangement” describes which of the following?
o: orthogonal arrangement
involutory arrangement
inverse formula
invertibility condition
items.s: orthogonal arrangement is a square arrangement whose transpose is also its undoing arrangement.

items.q: The statement “two arrangements related by an undoing array on one side and the array itself on the other” describes which of the following?
o: diagonalisable arrangement
power by diagonalisation
diagonalisation
similar arrangements
items.s: similar arrangements is two arrangements related by an undoing array on one side and the array itself on the other.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines algebraic multiplicity.
o: one of the three allowed changes: swapping rows, scaling a row, or adding a multiple of a row to another
how many times a value appears as a root of the expression in a single symbol
the relation between two arrangements that can be turned into each other by allowed row changes
the statement that the undoing arrangement equals the transposed signed values divided by the single number
items.s: algebraic multiplicity: how many times a value appears as a root of the expression in a single symbol. The other options describe row equivalence, elementary row operation, inverse formula.

items.q: Which of the following best describes vector space?
o: a set closed under addition and under scaling by numbers, obeying the usual algebraic laws
the number of nonzero rows in the fully simplified form of an arrangement
a square arrangement whose attached single number is not zero
the step of removing a common nonsingular factor written on the left of both sides
items.s: vector space: a set closed under addition and under scaling by numbers, obeying the usual algebraic laws. The other options describe nonsingular arrangement, rank, left cancellation.

items.q: exchange lemma may be defined as
o: the statement that a member of a spanning collection can be swapped for an outside member and still span
the square root of the number the member is assigned with itself
a sum of scalar multiples of a collection of members
the number left after deleting the row and the column that contain that entry
items.s: exchange lemma: the statement that a member of a spanning collection can be swapped for an outside member and still span. The other options describe linear combination, minor of an entry, norm of a member.

items.q: Which of the following best describes defective arrangement?
o: a square arrangement that is its own undoing arrangement
the set of values in which every unknown is zero
the statement that a member of a spanning collection can be swapped for an outside member and still span
a square arrangement that cannot be written in diagonal sandwich form because some value lacks enough members
items.s: defective arrangement: a square arrangement that cannot be written in diagonal sandwich form because some value lacks enough members. The other options describe exchange lemma, trivial solution, involutory arrangement.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines diagonal array.
o: a simplified arrangement in which each leading entry lies to the right of the one above it
the statement that the undoing arrangement equals the transposed signed values divided by the single number
a square arrangement whose entries off the leading diagonal are all zero
a square arrangement whose transpose is also its undoing arrangement
items.s: diagonal array: a square arrangement whose entries off the leading diagonal are all zero. The other options describe row echelon form, inverse formula, orthogonal arrangement.

items.q: Which term is described by “the square root of the number the member is assigned with itself”?
o: norm of a member
orthogonal members
orthogonal projection
Cauchy inequality
items.s: norm of a member is the square root of the number the member is assigned with itself.

items.q: All of the following belong to Matrices and matrix algebra EXCEPT
o: transpose
order of a rectangular array
zero member
symmetric array
items.s: Every other option belongs to Matrices and matrix algebra. “zero member” belongs to Vector spaces, not Matrices and matrix algebra.

items.q: Which of the following best describes algebraic multiplicity?
o: the requirement that the attached single number of the square arrangement is not zero
how many times a value appears as a root of the expression in a single symbol
a square arrangement that is its own undoing arrangement
a square arrangement with ones on the leading diagonal and zeros elsewhere
items.s: algebraic multiplicity: how many times a value appears as a root of the expression in a single symbol. The other options describe involutory arrangement, identity array, invertibility condition.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines orthonormal collection?
o: a square arrangement whose attached single number is not zero
the total of the entries on the leading diagonal of a square arrangement
a square arrangement in which every entry on one side of the leading diagonal is zero
a set of unit members that are pairwise orthogonal
items.s: orthonormal collection: a set of unit members that are pairwise orthogonal. The other options describe triangular array, nonsingular arrangement, trace.

items.q: triangular array may be defined as
o: the statement that a member of a spanning collection can be swapped for an outside member and still span
a square arrangement in which every entry on one side of the leading diagonal is zero
how many times a value appears as a root of the expression in a single symbol
a set of conditions that has at least one set of values satisfying them all
items.s: triangular array: a square arrangement in which every entry on one side of the leading diagonal is zero. The other options describe algebraic multiplicity, consistent system, exchange lemma.

items.q: orthogonal projection may be defined as
o: a square arrangement whose entries off the leading diagonal are all zero
the step of removing a common nonsingular factor written on the left of both sides
a part of a space that is itself a space under the same two operations
the part of a member lying along a chosen direction
items.s: orthogonal projection: the part of a member lying along a chosen direction. The other options describe subspace, left cancellation, diagonal array.

items.q: Which of the following best describes consistent system?
o: the statement that the count of columns equals the number of leading entries plus the count of columns without one
a set of conditions that has at least one set of values satisfying them all
a square array that is unchanged when its rows and columns are interchanged
the finding of a high power by raising only the diagonal factor to that power
items.s: consistent system: a set of conditions that has at least one set of values satisfying them all. The other options describe rank nullity relation, symmetric array, power by diagonalisation.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines involutory arrangement.
o: a simplified arrangement in which each leading entry is one and is the only nonzero entry in its column
a square arrangement that is its own undoing arrangement
the writing of a whole number as a sum of entries of one row each multiplied by their signed smaller values
a square arrangement whose attached single number is zero
items.s: involutory arrangement: a square arrangement that is its own undoing arrangement. The other options describe cofactor expansion, reduced row echelon form, singular arrangement.

items.q: Which term is described by “the whole collection of values attached to an arrangement”?
o: eigenspace
spectrum
eigenvector
geometric multiplicity
items.s: spectrum is the whole collection of values attached to an arrangement.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines spectrum?
o: the whole collection of values attached to an arrangement
an arrangement in which every entry is zero
the situation in which a square arrangement has two equal rows and so carries the number zero
a rule assigning a number to each ordered pair of members, symmetric and positive on each member with itself
items.s: spectrum: the whole collection of values attached to an arrangement. The other options describe inner product, null array, vanishing condition.

items.q: The statement “a sum of scalar multiples of a collection of members” describes which of the following?
o: exchange lemma
change of basis array
linear independence
linear combination
items.s: linear combination is a sum of scalar multiples of a collection of members.

items.q: norm of a member may be defined as
o: the number left after deleting the row and the column that contain that entry
the part of a member lying along a chosen direction
the square root of the number the member is assigned with itself
the single set of values that satisfies a consistent set of conditions
items.s: norm of a member: the square root of the number the member is assigned with itself. The other options describe unique solution, orthogonal projection, minor of an entry.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines inverse of a product?
o: two arrangements related by an undoing array on one side and the array itself on the other
two arrangements whose inner counts agree, so that they may be multiplied in that order
the reversal rule that undoing a chain of factors gives the individual undoings in the opposite order
a square arrangement in which every entry on one side of the leading diagonal is zero
items.s: inverse of a product: the reversal rule that undoing a chain of factors gives the individual undoings in the opposite order. The other options describe similar arrangements, triangular array, conformable pair.

items.q: cofactor expansion may be defined as
o: the set of all combinations of the columns of an arrangement
the writing of a whole number as a sum of entries of one row each multiplied by their signed smaller values
two members whose assigned number under the pairing rule is zero
the count of columns without a leading entry in the simplified form
items.s: cofactor expansion: the writing of a whole number as a sum of entries of one row each multiplied by their signed smaller values. The other options describe orthogonal members, column space, nullity.

items.q: The statement “the statement that the undoing arrangement equals the transposed signed values divided by the single number” describes which of the following?
o: involutory arrangement
invertibility condition
inverse formula
inverse
items.s: inverse formula is the statement that the undoing arrangement equals the transposed signed values divided by the single number.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines maximal independent set.
o: the step of removing a common nonsingular factor written on the left of both sides
a part of a space that is itself a space under the same two operations
a collection that is independent and cannot be enlarged without losing that property
the situation in which some combination with not all scalars zero gives the zero member
items.s: maximal independent set: a collection that is independent and cannot be enlarged without losing that property. The other options describe subspace, left cancellation, linear dependence.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines spanning set?
o: a collection whose combinations produce every member of the space
the total of the entries on the leading diagonal of a square arrangement
an unknown whose value may be chosen at will once the others are fixed
the number left after deleting the row and the column that contain that entry
items.s: spanning set: a collection whose combinations produce every member of the space. The other options describe trace, minor of an entry, free variable.

items.q: Which of the following best describes skew symmetric array?
o: a square array that becomes the negative of itself when its rows and columns are interchanged
an independent collection that also produces every member of the space
a square arrangement with ones on the leading diagonal and zeros elsewhere
the part of a member lying along a chosen direction
items.s: skew symmetric array: a square array that becomes the negative of itself when its rows and columns are interchanged. The other options describe basis, identity array, orthogonal projection.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines identity array?
o: a square arrangement whose entries off the leading diagonal are all zero
a square arrangement with ones on the leading diagonal and zeros elsewhere
the count of columns without a leading entry in the simplified form
the unique element that leaves every element unchanged when added to it
items.s: identity array: a square arrangement with ones on the leading diagonal and zeros elsewhere. The other options describe diagonal array, zero member, nullity.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines augmented array?
o: the count of its rows written together with the count of its columns
the square root of the number the member is assigned with itself
the finding of a high power by raising only the diagonal factor to that power
the arrangement of coefficients written beside the column of right hand values
items.s: augmented array: the arrangement of coefficients written beside the column of right hand values. The other options describe order of a rectangular array, norm of a member, power by diagonalisation.

items.q: Which of the following best describes minor of an entry?
o: two arrangements related by an undoing array on one side and the array itself on the other
the first nonzero entry in a row of a simplified array, used to clear the entries beneath it
the number left after deleting the row and the column that contain that entry
the writing of an arrangement as a product of a basis array, a diagonal array and the undoing of the basis array
items.s: minor of an entry: the number left after deleting the row and the column that contain that entry. The other options describe pivot, diagonalisation, similar arrangements.

items.q: reduced row echelon form may be defined as

the single number attached to a square arrangement that tells whether it can be undone
the list of scalars that expresses a member in terms of a chosen basis
a set of conditions in which every right hand value is zero
items.s: reduced row echelon form: a simplified arrangement in which each leading entry is one and is the only nonzero entry in its column. The other options describe coordinate vector, homogeneous system, determinant.

the set of values in which every unknown is zero
the fact that having all values different guarantees the arrangement can be written in diagonal sandwich form
the statement that a member of a spanning collection can be swapped for an outside member and still span

a set of conditions that has at least one set of values satisfying them all
two arrangements related by an undoing array on one side and the array itself on the other
a collection whose combinations produce every member of the space

items.q: Which of the following best describes transpose?

an arrangement in which every entry is zero
a set of conditions in which every right hand value is zero
the array obtained by writing the rows of a given array as columns
items.s: transpose: the array obtained by writing the rows of a given array as columns. The other options describe homogeneous system, null array, free variable.

o: the fact that having all values different guarantees the arrangement can be written in diagonal sandwich form
the single number attached to a square arrangement that tells whether it can be undone
a set of conditions that has at least one set of values satisfying them all
a square arrangement in which every entry on one side of the leading diagonal is zero
items.s: consistent system: a set of conditions that has at least one set of values satisfying them all. The other options describe distinct value condition, determinant, triangular array.

items.q: The statement “the relation between two arrangements that can be turned into each other by allowed row changes” describes which of the following?

rank nullity relation

the statement that the undoing arrangement equals the transposed signed values divided by the single number
the part of the space formed by the zero member together with all members belonging to one value
an unknown whose value may be chosen at will once the others are fixed

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines change of basis array.

the statement that the count of columns equals the number of leading entries plus the count of columns without one
the arrangement whose columns are the old coordinates of the new basis members
everything that is orthogonal to every member of a stated part

items.q: Which statement correctly defines linear dependence?
o: the count of its rows written together with the count of its columns
the situation in which some combination with not all scalars zero gives the zero member
the arrangement which, multiplied by the given one on either side, gives the identity
the part consisting of the zero member alone
items.s: linear dependence: the situation in which some combination with not all scalars zero gives the zero member. The other options describe trivial subspace, inverse, order of a rectangular array.

items.q: The statement “two arrangements whose inner counts agree, so that they may be multiplied in that order” describes which of the following?
o: conformable pair
square array
symmetric array
diagonal array

a set of unit members that are pairwise orthogonal
the setting to zero of the expression in a single symbol that arises from the diagonal subtraction
a number for which some nonzero member is carried to a multiple of itself
items.s: characteristic equation: the setting to zero of the expression in a single symbol that arises from the diagonal subtraction. The other options describe linear independence, orthonormal collection, eigenvalue.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines triangular array.
o: a square arrangement in which every entry on one side of the leading diagonal is zero
a square arrangement that is its own undoing arrangement
a square array that is unchanged when its rows and columns are interchanged
two arrangements related by an undoing array on one side and the array itself on the other
items.s: triangular array: a square arrangement in which every entry on one side of the leading diagonal is zero. The other options describe involutory arrangement, similar arrangements, symmetric array.

the statement that the assigned number of a pair never exceeds the product of the two lengths
a square arrangement whose entries off the leading diagonal are all zero
the single number attached to a square arrangement that tells whether it can be undone
items.s: similar arrangements: two arrangements related by an undoing array on one side and the array itself on the other. The other options describe determinant, diagonal array, Cauchy inequality.

trivial subspace
closed under addition

column space
rank

unique solution

the count of members in any basis of the space

the arrangement of coefficients written beside the column of right hand values
a square arrangement that cannot be written in diagonal sandwich form because some value lacks enough members
the count of columns without a leading entry in the simplified form

the writing of an arrangement as a product of a basis array, a diagonal array and the undoing of the basis array
everything that is orthogonal to every member of a stated part
the statement that a member of a spanning collection can be swapped for an outside member and still span
items.s: exchange lemma: the statement that a member of a spanning collection can be swapped for an outside member and still span. The other options describe diagonalisation, diagonalisable arrangement, orthogonal complement.

items.q: Find the determinant of [[2, 1, 1], [0, 1, 0], [0, -2, 4]].
items.s: Expanding along the first column leaves 2 times the two by two number 1 x 4, giving 8.

items.q: Find the top left entry of the inverse of [[3, 1], [3, 2]].
items.s: The determinant is 3, and the top left entry of the inverse is 2/3 = 0.6667.

items.q: A system is written as [[5, 3], [3, 2]] times the column of unknowns equals a column of constants. Find the determinant of the coefficient arrangement and so decide whether the system has a unique solution; state that determinant.
items.s: The determinant is (5)(2) - (3)(3) = 1, and a nonzero value means the solution is unique.

items.q: An arrangement has 5 columns and its reduced form has 3 nonzero rows. State its nullity.
items.s: Nullity = columns - rank = 5 - 3 = 2.

items.q: The list (4, 2) is written in the basis whose first member is (2, 0). Find the first coordinate in that basis.
items.s: The first basis member has zero second coordinate, so the first coordinate is 4/4 = 1.

items.q: A two by two arrangement has eigenvalues 2 and 3. State its determinant.
items.s: The determinant equals the product of the eigenvalues, which is 6.

items.q: A diagonal two by two arrangement has both diagonal entries equal to 2. Find the trace of its 3th power.
items.s: Each diagonal entry of the power is 2^3 = 8, so the trace is twice that, 16.

items.q: Find the norm of the member (1, 2, 2) under the usual rule.
items.s: The norm is the square root of the sum of squares 9, which is 3.

items.q: Given A = [[3, -2], [4, -5]] and B = [[-1, 1], [1, -5]], find the top left entry of AB.
items.s: The top left entry is row one of A times column one of B: 3 x -1 + -2 x 1 = -5.

items.q: Given A = [[5, 1], [-3, -3]] and the identity I of order two, find the top left entry of A + 2I.
items.s: Only the diagonal is touched, so the top left entry is 5 + 2 = 7.
The product is diagonal with entries 40, 28, 49, so its trace is their total 117.

items.q: A two by two arrangement A has determinant 3. Find the determinant of 3A.
items.s: Scaling every row of a two by two arrangement multiplies the number by 3^2, so the answer is 9.

items.q: Find the determinant of the upper triangular arrangement [[6, 7, 2], [0, 3, 5], [0, 0, 5]].
items.s: For a triangular arrangement the number is the product of the diagonal entries, here 90.

items.q: Find the determinant of [[4, 4, 3], [5, 6, 5], [0, 0, 0]].
items.s: The last row is entirely zero, so the determinant is 0.

items.q: Two square arrangements A and B of the same order have determinants 5 and 2. Find the determinant of AB.
items.s: The number attached to a product is the product of the numbers, so it is 10.

items.q: Find the bottom left entry of the inverse of [[5, 1], [3, 3]].
items.s: The bottom left entry of the undoing arrangement is minus the lower left entry over the determinant 12, giving -0.25.

items.q: A two by two arrangement has determinant 7. Find the determinant of its inverse.
items.s: The number attached to the undoing arrangement is the reciprocal of 7, which is 0.1429.

items.q: Solve for x and y from 4x + 5y = 20 together with y = 1, and state the value of 4x + 5y.
items.s: Substituting y = 1 gives 4x = 15, so x = 3.75 and the expression equals 20.

items.q: A system with coefficient arrangement [[1, 4], [2, 1]] has right hand column (6, 6). Using the determinant method, find the first unknown.
items.s: The first unknown is (6 x 1 - 4 x 6)/-7 = 2.57.

items.q: A homogeneous system of three equations in three unknowns has coefficient arrangement of determinant 3. State the value of the unknowns in the only solution it can have when the determinant is nonzero.
items.s: With a nonzero determinant the homogeneous system has only the trivial solution, so every unknown is 0.

items.q: The reduced form of a 4 by 5 arrangement has 1 nonzero rows. The remaining rows are entirely zero. State the rank.
items.s: The rank is the number of nonzero rows in the reduced form, which is 1.

items.q: State the dimension of the space of all arrangements with 4 rows and 2 columns.
items.s: Every entry can be chosen freely, so there are 4 x 2 = 8 independent entries.

items.q: A part of a space consists of all members whose first coordinate equals 4 times the second. State whether it is a subspace by giving the number 1 for yes and 0 for no.
items.s: The condition is preserved by addition and by scaling, and the zero member satisfies it, so the part is a subspace, recorded as 1.

items.q: Two members of the plane have coordinates (5, 2) and (3, 1). State 1 if they are independent and 0 if they are dependent.
items.s: The test value 5 x 1 - 2 x 3 = -1 is nonzero, so the two members are independent, recorded as 1.

items.q: A two by two arrangement has eigenvalues 1 and 2. State the trace of the arrangement.
items.s: The trace equals the total of the eigenvalues, which is 3.

items.q: The characteristic expression of a two by two arrangement is L^2 - 8L + 16, where L stands for the unknown number. State the smaller of the two values it produces when set to zero.
items.s: The expression factorises with roots 4 and 4, so the smaller is 4.

items.q: A two by two arrangement has one eigenvalue equal to -3 and the other equal to 2. State the trace of the arrangement.
items.s: The trace is the total of the two values, which is -1.

items.q: A two by two arrangement has eigenvalues 3 and 5. Find the determinant of its 3th power.
items.s: The eigenvalues of the power are 3^3 and 5^3, so the determinant is their product 3375.

items.q: Under the usual rule the number assigned to the members (5, -4, 2) and (-3, 4, 4) is the sum of the products of matching coordinates. Find that number.
items.s: Multiplying matching coordinates and adding gives -23.

items.q: The member (15, 15, 15) lies along the direction (5, 5, 5). Find the scalar multiple that expresses it in terms of that direction.
items.s: Matching coordinates are all 3 times as large, so the multiple is 3.

items.q: State the number assigned by the usual rule to the members (2, 1, 0) and (1, -2, 0).
items.s: The products of matching coordinates are 2 and -2, whose total is 0, so the two members are orthogonal.

items.q: Given A = [[9, 4, -2], [-5, 2, -2]], find the entry in row 1 and column 2 of the transpose of A.
items.s: The transpose writes rows as columns, so the entry asked for is the one in row 2 and column 1 of A, which is -5.

items.q: Find the determinant of [[3, 3, 4], [0, 2, 0], [0, 1, 3]].
items.s: Expanding along the first column leaves 3 times the two by two number 2 x 3, giving 18.

items.q: Find the top left entry of the inverse of [[2, 1], [3, 2]].
items.s: The determinant is 1, and the top left entry of the inverse is 2/1 = 2.

items.q: A system is written as [[1, 3], [3, 2]] times the column of unknowns equals a column of constants. Find the determinant of the coefficient arrangement and so decide whether the system has a unique solution; state that determinant.
items.s: The determinant is (1)(2) - (3)(3) = -7, and a nonzero value means the solution is unique.

items.q: An arrangement has 3 columns and its reduced form has 2 nonzero rows. State its nullity.
items.s: Nullity = columns - rank = 3 - 2 = 1.

items.q: State the dimension of the space of all polynomials of degree at most 3 together with the zero polynomial.
items.s: A basis is 1, x, and so on up to x^3, which is 4 members.

items.q: The list (6, 3) is written in the basis whose first member is (2, 0). Find the first coordinate in that basis.
items.s: The first basis member has zero second coordinate, so the first coordinate is 6/4 = 1.5.

items.q: A two by two arrangement has eigenvalues 3 and 5. State its determinant.
items.s: The determinant equals the product of the eigenvalues, which is 15.

items.q: A diagonal two by two arrangement has both diagonal entries equal to 2. Find the trace of its 5th power.
items.s: Each diagonal entry of the power is 2^5 = 32, so the trace is twice that, 64.

items.q: Given A = [[6, 2], [-1, -2]] and the identity I of order two, find the top left entry of A + 3I.
items.s: Only the diagonal is touched, so the top left entry is 6 + 3 = 9.
The product is diagonal with entries 40, 56, 36, so its trace is their total 132.

items.q: A two by two arrangement A has determinant 0. Find the determinant of 3A.
items.s: Scaling every row of a two by two arrangement multiplies the number by 3^2, so the answer is 0.

items.q: Find the determinant of the upper triangular arrangement [[3, 7, 2], [0, 5, 5], [0, 0, 3]].
items.s: For a triangular arrangement the number is the product of the diagonal entries, here 45.

items.q: Find the determinant of [[7, 7, 3], [8, 9, 5], [0, 0, 0]].
items.s: The last row is entirely zero, so the determinant is 0.

items.q: Two square arrangements A and B of the same order have determinants 3 and -5. Find the determinant of AB.
items.s: The number attached to a product is the product of the numbers, so it is -15.

items.q: Find the bottom left entry of the inverse of [[3, 3], [4, 2]].
items.s: The bottom left entry of the undoing arrangement is minus the lower left entry over the determinant -6, giving 0.6667.

items.q: Solve for x and y from 4x + 3y = 14 together with y = 2, and state the value of 4x + 3y.
items.s: Substituting y = 2 gives 4x = 8, so x = 2 and the expression equals 14.

items.q: A system with coefficient arrangement [[3, 1], [3, 3]] has right hand column (2, 3). Using the determinant method, find the first unknown.
items.s: The first unknown is (2 x 3 - 1 x 3)/6 = 0.5.

items.q: The reduced form of a 4 by 5 arrangement has 4 nonzero rows. The remaining rows are entirely zero. State the rank.
items.s: The rank is the number of nonzero rows in the reduced form, which is 4.

items.q: State the dimension of the space of all arrangements with 2 rows and 2 columns.
items.s: Every entry can be chosen freely, so there are 2 x 2 = 4 independent entries.

items.q: A space has dimension 3 and a collection of 3 members is given. State the number of members a basis of the space must contain.
items.s: Every basis of a space of dimension 3 contains exactly 3 members.

items.q: Two members of the plane have coordinates (3, 4) and (2, 4). State 1 if they are independent and 0 if they are dependent.
items.s: The test value 3 x 4 - 4 x 2 = 4 is nonzero, so the two members are independent, recorded as 1.

items.q: A two by two arrangement has eigenvalues 5 and 2. State the trace of the arrangement.
items.s: The trace equals the total of the eigenvalues, which is 7.

items.q: The characteristic expression of a two by two arrangement is L^2 - 11L + 30, where L stands for the unknown number. State the smaller of the two values it produces when set to zero.
items.s: The expression factorises with roots 6 and 5, so the smaller is 5.

items.q: A two by two arrangement has one eigenvalue equal to -3 and the other equal to 1. State the trace of the arrangement.
items.s: The trace is the total of the two values, which is -2.

items.q: Under the usual rule the number assigned to the members (5, 1, -1) and (5, -3, 4) is the sum of the products of matching coordinates. Find that number.
items.s: Multiplying matching coordinates and adding gives 18.

items.q: The member (3, 3, 12) lies along the direction (1, 1, 4). Find the scalar multiple that expresses it in terms of that direction.
items.s: Matching coordinates are all 3 times as large, so the multiple is 3.

items.q: State the number assigned by the usual rule to the members (1, 2, 0) and (2, -1, 0).
items.s: The products of matching coordinates are 2 and -2, whose total is 0, so the two members are orthogonal.

items.q: Find the largest value that the pairing number of the member (6, 0, 0) with any member of length 8 can take, giving the answer to three decimal places.
items.s: The length of the given member is 6, and by the Cauchy inequality the largest pairing number is the product of the lengths, 6 x 8 = 48.

a sum of scalar multiples of a collection of members

a rule assigning a number to each ordered pair of members, symmetric and positive on each member with itself
the square root of the number the member is assigned with itself
the part of a member lying along a chosen direction

a set of unit members that are pairwise orthogonal
the part of a member lying along a chosen direction

power by diagonalisation
defective arrangement
distinct value condition

square array
conformable pair
null array

homogeneous system
rank
reduced row echelon form

the expression in a single symbol obtained by subtracting that symbol from the diagonal before taking the number
a nonzero member that a given arrangement merely stretches or reverses
the setting to zero of the expression in a single symbol that arises from the diagonal subtraction
items.s: characteristic polynomial: the expression in a single symbol obtained by subtracting that symbol from the diagonal before taking the number. The other options describe eigenvalue, characteristic equation, eigenvector.

items.q: Which term is described by “a square arrangement whose attached single number is zero”?

singular arrangement
vanishing condition
triangular array

a part of a space that is itself a space under the same two operations
the unique element that leaves every element unchanged when added to it
the property that combining any two members of the set stays inside it

items.q: column space is best described as

the set of all combinations of the columns of an arrangement
the statement that the count of columns equals the number of leading entries plus the count of columns without one
the count of columns without a leading entry in the simplified form

spanning set
coordinate vector
dimension

power by diagonalisation
diagonalisation

items.q: The best definition of triangular array among these is

eigenvalue
characteristic equation

algebraic multiplicity
eigenvector
geometric multiplicity

the property that combining any two members of the set stays inside it
a collection whose combinations produce every member of the space
the unique element that leaves every element unchanged when added to it

elementary row operation

pivot

the transpose of the array of signed smaller values of a square arrangement

the square root of the number the member is assigned with itself
everything that is orthogonal to every member of a stated part

basis

change of basis array

the signed value of the smaller number left after removing the row and column of that entry
the number left after deleting the row and the column that contain that entry

a set of unit members that are pairwise orthogonal
the statement that the assigned number of a pair never exceeds the product of the two lengths

diagonalisable arrangement
power by diagonalisation

the writing of an arrangement as a product of a basis array, a diagonal array and the undoing of the basis array
the finding of a high power by raising only the diagonal factor to that power

items.q: Given A = [[-2, -4, 1], [9, -2, -1]], find the entry in row 1 and column 2 of the transpose of A.

items.q: Find the determinant of [[-1, 8], [-3, 1]].

items.q: Given A = [[2, 0], [-5, -1]] and B = [[2, -5], [-4, 3]], find the top left entry of AB.
items.s: The top left entry is row one of A times column one of B: 2 x 2 + 0 x -4 = 4.

items.q: Given A = [[9, -5, 5], [1, 2, 8]], find the entry in row 2 and column 2 of the transpose of A.
items.s: The transpose writes rows as columns, so the entry asked for is the one in row 2 and column 2 of A, which is 2.

items.q: Given A = [[-4, 2], [2, -1]] and the identity I of order two, find the top left entry of A + -2I.
items.s: Only the diagonal is touched, so the top left entry is -4 + -2 = -6.
The product is diagonal with entries 72, 20, 42, so its trace is their total 134.

items.q: Find the determinant of [[-3, 8], [-1, 6]].
items.s: For a two by two arrangement the number is (-3)(6) - (8)(-1) = -10.

items.q: Find the determinant of [[4, 3, 2], [0, 2, 0], [0, 1, 1]].
items.s: Expanding along the first column leaves 4 times the two by two number 2 x 1, giving 8.

items.q: Find the determinant of the upper triangular arrangement [[3, 7, 2], [0, 6, 5], [0, 0, 3]].
items.s: For a triangular arrangement the number is the product of the diagonal entries, here 54.

items.q: Find the determinant of [[7, 6, 3], [8, 8, 5], [0, 0, 0]].
items.s: The last row is entirely zero, so the determinant is 0.

items.q: Find the top left entry of the inverse of [[1, 3], [1, 4]].
items.s: The determinant is 1, and the top left entry of the inverse is 4/1 = 4.

items.q: Find the bottom left entry of the inverse of [[3, 1], [4, 5]].
items.s: The bottom left entry of the undoing arrangement is minus the lower left entry over the determinant 11, giving -0.3636.

items.q: A two by two arrangement has determinant -2. Find the determinant of its inverse.
items.s: The number attached to the undoing arrangement is the reciprocal of -2, which is -0.5.

items.q: Solve for x and y from 4x + 5y = 10 together with y = 2, and state the value of 4x + 5y.
items.s: Substituting y = 2 gives 4x = 0, so x = 0 and the expression equals 10.

items.q: A system is written as [[1, 5], [2, 1]] times the column of unknowns equals a column of constants. Find the determinant of the coefficient arrangement and so decide whether the system has a unique solution; state that determinant.
items.s: The determinant is (1)(1) - (5)(2) = -9, and a nonzero value means the solution is unique.

items.q: Two members of the plane have coordinates (1, 1) and (2, 3). State 1 if they are independent and 0 if they are dependent.
items.s: The test value 1 x 3 - 1 x 2 = 1 is nonzero, so the two members are independent, recorded as 1.

items.q: A two by two arrangement has eigenvalues -3 and 3. State its determinant.
items.s: The determinant equals the product of the eigenvalues, which is -9.

items.q: The characteristic expression of a two by two arrangement is L^2 - 7L + 10, where L stands for the unknown number. State the smaller of the two values it produces when set to zero.
items.s: The expression factorises with roots 5 and 2, so the smaller is 2.

items.q: A two by two arrangement has one eigenvalue equal to -4 and the other equal to 1. State the trace of the arrangement.
items.s: The trace is the total of the two values, which is -3.

items.q: A diagonal two by two arrangement has both diagonal entries equal to 2. Find the trace of its 4th power.
items.s: Each diagonal entry of the power is 2^4 = 16, so the trace is twice that, 32.

items.q: Under the usual rule the number assigned to the members (-3, 4, -1) and (0, -3, 5) is the sum of the products of matching coordinates. Find that number.
items.s: Multiplying matching coordinates and adding gives -17.

items.q: The member (4, 6, 4) lies along the direction (2, 3, 2). Find the scalar multiple that expresses it in terms of that direction.
items.s: Matching coordinates are all 2 times as large, so the multiple is 2.

items.q: Two square arrangements A and B of the same order have determinants -4 and 7. Find the determinant of AB.
items.s: The number attached to a product is the product of the numbers, so it is -28.

items.q: A system with coefficient arrangement [[4, 4], [4, 1]] has right hand column (6, 2). Using the determinant method, find the first unknown.
items.s: The first unknown is (6 x 1 - 4 x 2)/-12 = 0.1667.

items.q: State the number assigned by the usual rule to the members (3, 3, 0) and (3, -3, 0).
items.s: The products of matching coordinates are 9 and -9, whose total is 0, so the two members are orthogonal.

items.q: Find the largest value that the pairing number of the member (6, 0, 0) with any member of length 12.17 can take, giving the answer to three decimal places.
items.s: The length of the given member is 6, and by the Cauchy inequality the largest pairing number is the product of the lengths, 6 x 12.17 = 72.99.

items.q: Given A = [[-6, -2], [5, 1]] and B = [[-5, -3], [3, -3]], find the top left entry of AB.

items.q: Given A = [[-4, 1], [2, 0]] and the identity I of order two, find the top left entry of A + 3I.

items.q: Find the determinant of [[3, 6], [3, -5]].
items.s: For a two by two arrangement the number is (3)(-5) - (6)(3) = -33.

items.q: Find the determinant of [[1, -1, 4], [0, 2, 0], [0, 3, 2]].
items.s: Expanding along the first column leaves 1 times the two by two number 2 x 2, giving 4.

items.q: A two by two arrangement A has determinant 8. Find the determinant of 4A.
items.s: Scaling every row of a two by two arrangement multiplies the number by 4^2, so the answer is 32.

items.q: Find the determinant of the upper triangular arrangement [[5, 7, 2], [0, 4, 5], [0, 0, 6]].
items.s: For a triangular arrangement the number is the product of the diagonal entries, here 120.

items.q: Find the determinant of [[2, 7, 3], [3, 9, 5], [0, 0, 0]].
items.s: The last row is entirely zero, so the determinant is 0.

items.s: The determinant is 7, and the top left entry of the inverse is 4/7 = 0.5714.

items.q: The correct meaning of symmetric array is
o: a square array that is unchanged when its rows and columns are interchanged
an arrangement with the same count of rows as of columns
the total of the entries on the leading diagonal of a square arrangement
two arrangements whose inner counts agree, so that they may be multiplied in that order
items.s: symmetric array: a square array that is unchanged when its rows and columns are interchanged. The other options describe square array, conformable pair, trace.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a set of unit members that are pairwise orthogonal”
o: inner product
orthogonal complement
Cauchy inequality
orthonormal collection
items.s: orthonormal collection is a set of unit members that are pairwise orthogonal.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the square root of the number the member is assigned with itself”
o: Cauchy inequality
Gram determinant
orthogonal complement
norm of a member
items.s: norm of a member is the square root of the number the member is assigned with itself.

items.q: The correct meaning of inconsistent system is
o: a set of conditions that has at least one set of values satisfying them all
the arrangement of coefficients written beside the column of right hand values
a set of conditions in which every right hand value is zero
a set of conditions that no set of values can satisfy together
items.s: inconsistent system: a set of conditions that no set of values can satisfy together. The other options describe consistent system, homogeneous system, augmented array.

items.q: In this course, rank refers to
o: the number of nonzero rows in the fully simplified form of an arrangement
a simplified arrangement in which each leading entry is one and is the only nonzero entry in its column
the count of columns without a leading entry in the simplified form
the relation between two arrangements that can be turned into each other by allowed row changes
items.s: rank: the number of nonzero rows in the fully simplified form of an arrangement. The other options describe nullity, reduced row echelon form, row equivalence.

items.q: The correct meaning of vanishing condition is
o: the situation in which a square arrangement has two equal rows and so carries the number zero
the single number attached to a square arrangement that tells whether it can be undone
a square arrangement whose attached single number is zero
the signed value of the smaller number left after removing the row and column of that entry
items.s: vanishing condition: the situation in which a square arrangement has two equal rows and so carries the number zero. The other options describe singular arrangement, cofactor of an entry, determinant.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines free variable?
o: a set of conditions that has at least one set of values satisfying them all
an unknown whose value may be chosen at will once the others are fixed
a set of conditions in which every right hand value is zero
a set of conditions that no set of values can satisfy together
items.s: free variable: an unknown whose value may be chosen at will once the others are fixed. The other options describe consistent system, inconsistent system, homogeneous system.

items.q: The correct meaning of coordinate vector is
o: the unique element that leaves every element unchanged when added to it
the part consisting of the zero member alone
the list of scalars that expresses a member in terms of a chosen basis
a part of a space that is itself a space under the same two operations
items.s: coordinate vector: the list of scalars that expresses a member in terms of a chosen basis. The other options describe trivial subspace, zero member, subspace.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains inverse.
o: the statement that the undoing arrangement equals the transposed signed values divided by the single number
the arrangement which, multiplied by the given one on either side, gives the identity
the step of removing a common nonsingular factor written on the left of both sides
a square arrangement whose transpose is also its undoing arrangement
items.s: inverse: the arrangement which, multiplied by the given one on either side, gives the identity. The other options describe left cancellation, inverse formula, orthogonal arrangement.
